blocks.x: Twins earn budget by improving named decisions against named baselines.
The twin is a decision instrument, not a 3D screenshot. Physics + data hybrids validate against measured reality — or the twin is fiction.
Configuration governance recalibrates when the asset changes; drift monitoring keeps it honest.
Scenario engines (what-if, sensitivity) are where planners actually live.
Where it breaks in practice: the demo gap: pilots on curated feeds, production on messy reality — and a twin that drifts from the asset until operators stop opening it.
The serious opposition goes: the twin-first thesis can produce beautiful models of assets nobody needed simulated. The twin earns its keep on the decisions it changes, not the fidelity it displays.

In delivery, this thesis becomes a specific discipline: the physical layer gets wired to the decision loop — sensor fabric, edge processing, and digital twins that stay synchronized with reality. Every program in the IoT, Twin & Robotics domain carries the same obligations — a signed baseline, named gate criteria, and evidence generated by running the system rather than preparing for a meeting.
A value assessment prices the delta in your estate before anything is signed: the twin is a decision instrument, not a 3D screenshot, measured against your baseline, in two weeks.
